notes: Loop 1: 7.2. Far less load now. Scenario cards show guess, result and one sentence, with the working folded (report-phone.png, step 3). The slider chart marks both thresholds (11 solid, 7 dashed). 'Warum sich das geändert hat' names the slope ('3 Gäste mehr × 5,35 € × 10 Tage = +160,50 €', ui-slider-explains). 'Was heißt …?' hints sit at the point of use, and the phone report is 11,763 px (was 23,943). Defects a learner still meets: (1) The predict box sits directly above a chart labelled 'Break-even: 11' (report-slider-moved.png, box empty). (2) On the landing, the step-4 mini chart puts the break-even dot off the line (site/index.html:145: the line crosses zero at x≈93, the dot is at x=122) and clips 'Gewinnschwelle:' at 390 px; in step 3, 'vorsichtig' collides with '−385 €' (landing-phone.png). (3) Chip names differ between landing and report (Erdacht/Ausgedacht; ES suposición/estimación; PL Wymyślone/Wyobrażone). (4) On the phone the facts card is closed while 'Mehrwertsteuer 10,6 % · Eine Schätzung' sits in the highlighted guesses box. (5) Three interview pairs give identical answers (report.txt:476-511). /try is one question per screen with a 'why' and a demo placeholder, but 13 optional fields hide in one collapsed panel.
improvements: Step 4, src/report/sections.ts step4 explorer and src/report/mount.ts:226 cover(): until the owner guesses or taps 'Einfach zeigen', give the explorer's two markers ('Break-even: 11', 'Trägt sich: 7'), the last clause of the 'Warum sich das geändert hat' text and the 'Gut zu wissen' callout the same data-wi-be-cover treatment as the big number. Or render the explorer below the reveal only. Why: the predict-then-check moment is the report's one active-learning step, and today the answer is in view on a 390 px screen. It worked when report-phone.png, scrolled to the empty predict box, shows no '11' or '7' in the next 844 px, and both markers appear after a guess.

Landing method visuals, site/index.html:145 and site/src/home.ts:177. Redraw the step-4 line so it passes through the dot ('M8 96 L212 24' crosses y=56 at x=122). Place the label where German fits inside the 220 viewBox (left-anchored in the green zone, or the shorter 'Gewinnschwelle 11/Tag'). In the step-3 mini chart, reserve a label column so 'vorsichtig' and '−385 €' do not overlap. Why: the landing is the advance organiser. Its one break-even picture must show the rule the report teaches (where the line crosses zero), and a clipped number teaches nothing. It worked when landing-phone.png shows the dot on the line and the full 'Gewinnschwelle: 11 pro Tag'.

One vocabulary per concept: site/src/lib/messages-de.ts c.src_imagined 'Erdacht' vs report src.imagined 'Ausgedacht'; m.s4/m.be 'Gewinnschwelle' vs report step4 'Break-even'; m.stop 'Aufhören' vs tc.stop 'Beenden'; report predict.lowOngoing 'Einrichtung' vs 'Startkosten'. Likewise ES c.src_assumption/c.src_demo and PL c.src_calculation/c.src_imagined/c.src_demo and m.s4 'próg opłacalności' vs report 'próg rentowności'. Have the site import chip names from REPORT_MESSAGES. In German pick 'Gewinnschwelle (Break-even)' once, then one word. Why: the four source labels are the AI lesson's vocabulary. A learner meeting two names for one label, or two names for the break-even, carries extra load and may think they are different things. It worked when a check asserts site c.src_* equals report src.* per language, and report.txt and landing.txt name the break-even and the stop verdict the same way.

Step 2, src/report/sections.ts step2 guesses box and src/report/mount.ts:98 (data-wi-open-wide is desktop only). Take the blended VAT row out of 'Schätzungen, die noch niemand kennt … Ihr Test prüft sie' and show it as 'Ihre Mischung Speisen/Getränke (geschätzt 70/30) → 10,6 %', with a fact chip for 7 %/19 % and a guess chip for the mix. Open 'Verwendete Berlin-Fakten' by default on phones, or put the two rates with 'Stand: 1. Januar 2026' inline under that row. Why: the facts card should teach that some numbers are public, dated rules, yet the first thing a phone reader sees is VAT labelled a guess her test will check. It worked when report-phone.png shows the 7 %/19 % rates with source and date without a tap, and the test-checks box holds only things the test measures.

/try review screen, site/src/try.ts:528-575 ('Genauer machen (optional)', 13 fields in one collapsed panel). Turn it into two or three optional screens, each with one why: 'Was gibt ein Mittagsgast aus?' (at minimum lunch spend, which the report ranks second in 'Welche Schätzung am meisten zählt'), 'Was kostet Sie der Test?' (setup, staff hours, promotion) and 'Wie viele Stammgäste würden wechseln?'. Each gets 'Weiß ich nicht — überspringen'. Why: one question per screen is the wizard's own scaffold, and a wall of 13 fields is where an owner stops reading and accepts defaults. Here the defaults (0 € setup, 0 staff hours, lunch spend = 7,40 € average) make the break-even 0. It worked when try-walkthrough.txt lists the new screens and ui-try-keyboard still passes.

Step 5, src/sim (interview) and src/report/rehearsal.ts 'In ihren Worten'. Three pairs of imagined customers give word-for-word identical interview answers (Chiara = Paweł, Noor = Greta, Murat = Jan, report.txt:479-511). Show each answer once with 'sagten 2 Gäste', or vary them by persona. Also align 'Fragen an drei oder vier echte Gäste' with 'Fragen Sie fünf Stammgäste' (report.txt:340-342). Why: identical quotes from different 'people' undercut the lesson that the personas differ in ways that matter, and two different counts on one card cost the reader a second look. It worked when no interview text repeats in report.txt and the checklist uses one number.
misconceptionsRisked: Break-even is not where the result line crosses zero (landing step-4 mini chart, dot off the line, site/index.html:145).
VAT is a guess the test will check: the 'Eine Schätzung' VAT row sits in the highlighted guesses box, and the dated facts card is closed on the phone (report-phone.png, step 2).
'Erdacht' and 'Ausgedacht', or 'Break-even' and 'Gewinnschwelle', are different labels or different numbers (landing.txt vs report.txt).
Imagined customers are interchangeable: three identical interview pairs (report.txt:479-511).
The demo's measured result is the owner's own number: chip 'Ihre Zahl' on made-up counts in the after-test demo (src/report/sections.ts:650).
scaffoldingGaps: On the phone the predict box and the answer share one screen.
Step 1 still previews −118 €, −546 € and 36 %, plus four counts in 'Wer hat was gemacht?' and four numbers in options A/B, before step 2 introduces any input (report.txt:53-97).
Step 4's title is still singular ('Die Zahl zum Merken') while the card, chart and test card use two thresholds.
The /try optional details are one 13-field panel, not screens with a 'why' each.
'Gut zu wissen' (the switching-regulars mechanism) and the Berlin facts card are closed by default on the phone; the one hands-on control moves only extra customers.
languageLoad: On screen the German report is as compact as the English (11,763 px vs 10,907 px at 390 px), with correct formats (9,90 €, 1.500 €, 22.481 €) and 'Sie' throughout. Its extra load is labels: chart and stepper say 'Break-even', the landing and closing lessons say 'Gewinnschwelle'; landing chip 'Erdacht' vs report chip 'Ausgedacht'; 'Aufhören' (landing) vs 'Beenden' (test card). The German label 'Gewinnschwelle:' is also clipped in the landing's mini chart at 390 px. Polish reads naturally ('Próg rentowności', '1500 €' per Polish grouping), but its landing uses other words for the same chips and for the break-even. Spanish is consistent apart from the 'Una suposición'/'Una estimación' chip.
